content: The time spent reassuring respondents and addressing their questions is critical. In addition to the BeSD survey questions outlined above, countries may choose to include additional questions regarding the provision of COVID-19 vaccines. These questions are specifically designed for health workers and should only be included in data collection if they provide valuable descriptive data for the immunization program. Willingness to Recommend Vaccines to Others Health workers may be asked, Would you recommend a COVID-19 vaccine to eligible individuals? The percentage of health workers who respond affirmatively (yes) will be measured. This question evaluates the willingness of health workers to recommend or promote COVID-19 vaccines to eligible candidates. If COVID-19 vaccines are not yet available in a country, the question can be adapted to: Would you recommend a COVID-19 vaccine to eligible individuals when it becomes available? Confidence in Answering Patient Questions Health workers may also be asked, How confident are you that you could answer patient questions about getting a COVID-19 vaccine? The percentage of health workers who report being moderately or very confident will be measured. This question assesses the confidence of health workers in their ability to address patients' informational needs regarding COVID-19 vaccines once they become available. If vaccines are not yet available, the question can be adapted to: How confident are you that you could answer patient questions about getting a COVID-19 vaccine, once it is available? Response options may include: Not at all confident, A little confident, Moderately confident, or Very confident. Perceived Risk of COVID-19 Participants may be asked, How concerned are you about getting COVID-19? Probing questions may include: Why do you feel that way? and How likely do you think it is? This question aims to understand the participant's perceived risk of contracting COVID-19 (the disease, not the vaccine). It also ties into later questions about their willingness to receive a COVID-19 vaccine when available. Perceived Risk to Patients Participants may be asked, What do you think about the risk that you could give COVID-19 to your patients? This question seeks to understand the participant's perceived risk of transmitting the virus to others. COVID-19 Stigma Health workers may be asked, As a health-care worker, how are you usually treated by others in the community? Probing questions may include: Have you noticed anything different in how you’re treated since the pandemic? This question enables exploration of the presence or experience of stigma related to COVID-19. COVID-19 Vaccine Information Participants may be asked, What have you heard about the COVID-19 vaccine(s)? Probing questions may include: Have you heard anything that worries you? Who did you hear this from? and Do you think it’s true? Why? This question aims to gather information about the participant's exposure to vaccine-related information and their concerns or beliefs about its accuracy. COVID-19 Vaccine Confidence Participants may be asked, How do you feel about the COVID-19 vaccine(s)? Probing questions may include: If multiple vaccines are available, what are the perceptions of each? What are your thoughts about the safety of the vaccine? and Do you have concerns about how 'new' the vaccines are? This question elicits the participant's confidence in the vaccine, covering aspects such as safety, efficacy, and alignment with personal or religious beliefs. COVID-19 Vaccine Intention Participants may be asked, Have you thought about getting a COVID-19 vaccine? What did you decide? Why? This question seeks to understand their intentions and decisions regarding vaccination. Responses may serve as a cross-check to previous answers and provide deeper insight into their motivations. Decision-Making Process for Vaccination Participants may be asked, Take me through how you will or have decided whether to get a COVID-19 vaccine. Probing questions may include: Was anyone else involved in the decision? and Who did you discuss it with? This question explores the decision-making process, including autonomy and the influence of social factors. Impact of Vaccination on Social Interactions Participants who have already received the vaccine may be asked, Has getting a COVID-19 vaccine changed things for you? Those who have not yet received the vaccine may be asked, How do you think getting a COVID-19 vaccine might change things for you? This question explores the perceived or actual impact of vaccination on their lives, including social interactions. Accessing the COVID-19 Vaccine Participants may be asked, Can you take me through how you would get or how you got a COVID-19 vaccine? Start at the beginning. Probing questions may include: Would/did you need to ask permission? Where would/did you go to get it? How would/did you get there? and Would there be/was there any cost involved for you (e.g., transport)? This question aims to understand the logistical and practical challenges of accessing the vaccine and what might make it easier for them. Cognitive Interviewing for Survey Adaptation Cognitive interviewing is recommended to improve the quality of survey translations and ensure questions and response options are well-adapted to the local context. This process involves recruiting participants from the target population, such as parents or caregivers of children under five, and conducting interviews to test and refine survey questions. Each question and its response options should be reviewed individually, with interviews lasting approximately 2–3 minutes per question.
